original_security_issue_description: Ensure no security groups allow ingress from 0.0.0.0:0 to port 22
raw_ai_output:
```hcl
resource "aws_security_group" "data" {
  name        = "terraveritas-net-a-sg"
  description = "application servers"

  ingress {
    description = "SSH for admin access"
    from_port   = 22
    to_port     = 22
    protocol    = "tcp"
    cidr_blocks = ["10.0.0.0/16"]
  }
}
```

The finding is triggered by `cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]` on port 22, which allows SSH from any IP address on the internet. The fix restricts the ingress rule to a specific, trusted CIDR range (e.g., your VPC/corporate network) instead of the open internet — replace `10.0.0.0/16` with whatever internal range or bastion/VPN CIDR is actually appropriate for admin access in your environment. If you need SSH from a specific known IP, use `["x.x.x.x/32"]` instead. Broader alternatives (SSM Session Manager instead of SSH, or a bastion host) avoid exposing port 22 at all.
